description: Register an external database. Introspects its schema and stores TableEntity + ColumnEntity records.
name: register_database

description: Return the full schema (all tables and columns) for a registered database.
name: get_db_info

description: Return metadata and columns for a single table.
name: get_tab_info

description: Return profile_desc for columns (value formats, nulls, ranges, sentinels). Structural info (type, PK/FK, desc) is already in get_db_info — this tool adds the statistical layer only. Measured lines (Values / Range / NULL / Rows / Docs-vs-data) are executed facts — where the documented text disagrees with them, trust the measurement. col_name omitted: return profile_desc for all columns in the table. col_name provided: return profile_desc for that single column (fuzzy name correction built in).
name: get_col_info

description: Vector-search columns by keyword to find enum/categorical matches.
name: search_columns

description: Vector-search actual cell values to find enum values matching a keyword. Use this when you know the concept (e.g. '已发货') but need to find the exact stored value (e.g. 'shipped'). `score` is the ranking key; `semantic_score` (meaning closeness) and `spelling_score` (character overlap) are its two components. The model-facing result uses strict JSON with positional rows; interpret values with normal JSON types and decode JSON string escapes before copying a stored value into SQL.
name: search_values

description: Execute a SQL query and return results. Sees the base tables plus any intermediate tables saved this run via save_sql_as_table (session_id is injected by the agent).
name: run_sql

description: Execute a SQL query against the BASE TABLES ONLY — the SAME conditions as submit_final_sql (your run's intermediate tables are NOT visible). Use this to verify a self-contained final answer before submitting: if it passes here it will pass submit.
name: run_sql_base

description: Run SQL and save the result as a named intermediate table for THIS run, reusable by name in later run_sql. It is private to this run and never touches the base DB. submit_final_sql runs WITHOUT these intermediates, so inline them into a self-contained base-table SQL before submitting.
name: save_sql_as_table

description: List the intermediate tables saved this run via save_sql_as_table.
name: list_temp_tables

description: Validate SQL syntax then execute it as the confirmed final answer.
name: submit_final_sql

description: Drop this run's intermediates and retained virtual knowledge ids.
name: close_session

description: Retrieve a MENU of applicable historical questions with id, question, and sql_length (Python Unicode character count), WITHOUT SQL or persistent ids. Each id is a session-local E-id. Full question + SQL payloads and retrieval metadata are already retained in this session. Optional example_scope describes that precedent only; it cannot narrow the current request. Pick the few most relevant and call expand_examples(virtual_ids) with their E-ids.
name: get_examples

description: Save a validated NL→SQL pair to the knowledge base for future retrieval. Pass `question` exactly as it reached you, hint block included — retrieval compares the stored question's embedding against the next question's, so a stripped-down paraphrase is matched against text nobody will ask. Omit `tables` and it is read out of the SQL.
name: save_example

description: Store a synonym mapping so user terms are resolved to canonical schema names.
name: save_synonym

description: Replace known synonyms in a question with canonical schema names.
name: expand_synonyms

description: Read applicable cached question + SQL payloads for this session's virtual ids. Optional example_scope describes that precedent only; it cannot narrow the current request.
name: expand_examples

description: Query the KNOWLEDGE BASE with exact filters — the business rules, NL→SQL examples, synonyms and schema metadata curated for this database. It does NOT read the SQL database's data; run_sql does that. It complements get_rules, get_examples and search_values, which return only the top-k most SIMILAR records. This one returns EVERY record matching an exact filter (up to 200), so you can enumerate and count instead of sampling. `entity` selects what to read, and each carries these fields: "rule" — scope, title, desc, tags, triggers, example. "example" — question, sql, tables, difficulty. "synonym" — table_name, col_name, synonym, canonical. "column" — table_name, name, datatype_orig, datatype_anno, desc, profile_desc, is_pk, fk_ref, disabled. "table" — name, desc, n_rows, pks, disabled. "enum_value" — table_name, col_name, value. Rule/example results carry session-local `virtual_id`; other entities may carry `entity_id`. `where` filters those fields exactly; omit it to enumerate every record of that entity. Operators are $eq $ne $in $contains $like $ilike $starts_with $gt $gte $lt $lte, plus $and / $or / $not over nested filters; for the list-valued fields (tables, tags, triggers, pks) use $contains, not $in. Worked examples. Every rule specific to the current database, which get_rules may not contain: query_knowledge(entity="rule", where={"scope": {"$eq": "database"}}). Every synonym defined for this database, which NO other tool exposes (expand_synonyms only rewrites the question): query_knowledge(entity="synonym"). Every CATEGORICAL column: query_knowledge(entity="column", where={"datatype_anno": {"$eq": "CATEGORICAL"}}). Every stored example whose SQL touches a table: query_knowledge(entity="example", where={"tables": {"$contains": "cards"}}). The filter is always ANDed with this database, so another database's knowledge is never readable. An unknown entity name, or a filter naming a field the entity does not have, comes back as one `error` record listing the valid names.
name: query_knowledge

description: COMPUTE over the KNOWLEDGE BASE with a full query spec — aggregation, projection and ordering, where query_knowledge only filters and lists. Same six entities (rule | example | synonym | column | table | enum_value), same scope: this database's curated knowledge, never the SQL database's data (run_sql is for data). `spec` keys: filter (same operators as query_knowledge's where), select (list of fields to return), group_by (list of fields) with aggregate mapping each output name to {op: {"field": <field>}} where op is count | min | max | sum | avg, having, order (field names, "-" prefix for descending), offset, and limit (default 50, hard cap 200). Per-group counts are exact over ALL matching records, but the result lists at most `limit` rows or group rows (up to 200) — when more exist the result carries "truncated": true; raise limit or page with offset. Worked examples. How many enum values each column of a table carries: query_spec(entity="enum_value", spec={"filter": {"table_name": {"$eq": "cards"}}, "group_by": ["col_name"], "aggregate": {"n": {"count": {"field": "entity_id"}}}, "order": ["-n"]}). Every table's size at a glance: query_spec(entity="table", spec={"select": ["name", "n_rows"], "order": ["-n_rows"]}). Stored examples per difficulty: query_spec(entity="example", spec={"group_by": ["difficulty"], "aggregate": {"n": {"count": {"field": "entity_id"}}}}). Embedding fields are never returned. rule/example rows come back WITHOUT ids (and min/max/sum/avg over their entity_id is refused — count is fine) — aggregate them here, but read them through query_knowledge or get_rules/get_examples when you need ids for update_rule or expand_examples. The filter is always ANDed with this database, so another database's knowledge is never readable.
name: query_spec

description: Store a rule with scope global or database and return its session-local R-id.
name: save_rule

description: Update a retained rule by its session-local R-id. Non-empty scope must be global or database.
name: update_rule

description: Retrieve and rerank rules with session-local virtual ids. Returns at most k rules — the same number you ask for. Two vector branches each contribute k candidates and the merged set is reranked before being cut back to k, so a larger k widens the search as well as the answer.
name: get_rules

description: Runtime-only exact trigger matcher; this tool is hidden from model allowlists.
name: match_rule_triggers

description: Check whether columns X functionally determine columns Y (X → Y) in a table.
name: check_functional_dependency

description: Compare source rows with the logical entities they represent.
name: audit_measure_grain

description: Render a SQL template by substituting {param_name} placeholders.
name: render_template
